grammar.title: Simple Sentences & be Verbs
goals: Understand what makes a complete sentence: it must have a subject and a verb and express a full idea.
Learn to find and fix sentence fragments.
Tell action verbs apart from state verbs.
Use “It” to talk about weather and time, e.g., It snows a lot.
Master the present forms of be: am, is, are.
Write three be‐verb sentence patterns: Subject + be + adjective; Subject + be + noun; Subject + be + prepositional phrase of place.
grammar.pacing: 老师根据掌握情况调整语法进度；阅读范围按本课大纲执行。
examples: Knight is a runner. → 主语 + be + 名词。
The shoes are light. → 主语 + be + 形容词。
I am ready. / He is ready. / They are ready. → be 随主语变化。
The shoes are in the box. → 主语 + be + 地点介词短语。
It is cold. / It is nine o’clock. → 天气或时间用 It 作主语。
× A new company. → ✓ It is a new company. → 片段补上主语与动词；He runs. 表动作，He knows the answer. 表状态。

exercises.explanation: shoes 是复数，使用 are。
完整句需要主语、动词和完整意思。
shoes 是复数，使用 are；in the box 表示地点。

exercises.prompt: Choose the sentence about the weather.
exercises.explanation: 天气句需要主语 It 和动词 is，后接形容词 cold。

notes.heading: 精读范围 · 按老师大纲
notes.text: Part 1 1962

notes.heading: 课前准备 · 系统学习建议
notes.text: 读完本课指定章节，用自己的话整理主要事件、人物的选择及其原因。补充问题仅用于帮助理解，不代表老师布置的作业。

questions.text: How does Knight turn his shoe-importing idea into an agreement with Onitsuka in 1962? Explain two steps he takes before any shoes arrive.
questions.reference_answer: Knight first obtains his father’s support and travels to Japan. He presents his idea to Onitsuka, describes an opportunity in the American running-shoe market, and seeks samples. The agreement grows from preparation and an actual meeting, even though he has not yet built a functioning company. Explain how the steps turn an idea into a possible business; do not describe later sales as if they have already happened.

questions.text: Why does asking his father for support feel difficult for Knight? What does the conversation reveal about both men?
questions.reference_answer: Knight wants his father’s practical and financial support but anticipates doubts about an uncertain venture. His father values a respectable, secure future, while Knight is drawn to travel and an untested opportunity. Their conversation reveals both the influence of family approval and Knight’s effort to act despite uncertainty. Other interpretations are valid when grounded in the conversation.

questions.text: When Onitsuka asks for his company’s name, Knight invents Blue Ribbon. How does the difference between the company name and his actual situation create tension?
questions.reference_answer: The name sounds like an established organization, although Knight has no such operating company. The reader knows how improvised the answer is, so the successful presentation carries both excitement and uncertainty. This gap highlights quick thinking as well as the risk of making a promise he must later turn into reality.

questions.text: Was Knight prepared enough to approach Onitsuka, or did he take too large a risk? Give your view using one preparation and one uncertainty from 1962.
questions.reference_answer: A supported answer can argue either side. His business-school work and knowledge of running give the proposal some foundation, while his lack of an established company, distribution network, or delivered samples leaves major uncertainty. Weigh a concrete preparation against a specific risk rather than claiming later success proves every early choice was sound.

lessons.title: Prepositional Phrases, There be & Punctuation Rules

grammar.title: Prepositional Phrases, There be & Punctuation Rules
goals: Understand prepositional phrases and tell place phrases from time phrases.
When a sentence has both place and time, put the place phrase before the time phrase.
Add a comma after a time phrase at the beginning of a sentence.
Use There is and There are to show that something exists in a place.
Capitalize the first word of every sentence, proper nouns, days, months, names, and book titles; end sentences with a period.
Practice combining two short sentences into one smoother sentence.
grammar.pacing: 老师根据掌握情况调整语法进度；阅读范围按本课大纲执行。
examples: There are two shoes in the box. → There are + 复数名词。
In the morning, he works in Oregon. → 句首时间短语后加逗号。
There is a shoe in the box. / There are two shoes in the box. → 单数 is，复数 are。
He works in the office every morning. → 地点在前，时间在后。
He works in Oregon. He sells shoes in Oregon. → He works and sells shoes in Oregon. → 合并重复信息。
× on monday, he works. → ✓ On Monday, he works. → 句首与星期名首字母大写；句末用句号。

exercises.prompt: There ___ a box in the office.
exercises.explanation: a box 是单数，使用 There is。

exercises.prompt: Choose the sentence with standard punctuation.
exercises.explanation: 句首与星期名称首字母大写，句首时间短语后按本课规则加逗号。

exercises.prompt: Choose the sentence with the usual place–time order.
options: She works in every morning the office.
She works in the office every morning.
She works the office in every morning.
exercises.explanation: 动词后先放地点 in the office，再放时间 every morning；地点介词 in 要紧接 the office。

options: He works and sells shoes in Oregon.
He works and selling shoes in Oregon.
He work and sells shoes in Oregon.
exercises.explanation: 同一主语 he 后并列动词保持一致：works 和 sells。

notes.heading: 精读范围 · 按老师大纲
notes.text: Part 1 1964 + Part 1 1963

notes.heading: 课前准备 · 系统学习建议
notes.text: 读完本课指定章节，用自己的话整理主要事件、人物的选择及其原因。补充问题仅用于帮助理解，不代表老师布置的作业。

questions.text: Across 1963 and 1964, what changes after the sample shoes finally arrive? Explain how Bowerman’s involvement helps turn waiting into a business.
questions.reference_answer: In 1963 Knight waits for samples while earning a living as an accountant and writing to Japan. When the shoes arrive in 1964, he can show and sell a real product. Bowerman’s interest leads to a partnership, adding coaching experience, product knowledge, credibility, and shared commitment. Explain the change using both years, even though the course lists 1964 before 1963.

questions.text: Why is Bowerman a particularly valuable partner for Knight? Explain how their strengths complement each other.
questions.reference_answer: Knight brings the importing idea and the drive to build distribution; Bowerman understands runners, coaching, and shoe performance. His participation offers more than money because he can judge and improve what runners need. A good explanation connects one of these strengths to a concrete action in the reading.

questions.text: How does the contrast between Knight’s accounting work and his enthusiasm for selling shoes help us understand him?
questions.reference_answer: Accounting provides income and a recognizable career, while the shoe venture gives Knight a much stronger sense of purpose. The contrast shows the distance between financial security and personal commitment. Explain the effect through his waiting, work, or early selling rather than treating all paid work as unimportant.

questions.text: If you advised Knight during the long wait in 1963, what practical next step would you suggest? Use what happens by 1964 to explain your advice.
questions.reference_answer: Reasonable advice might combine continued paid work with persistent contact, careful preparation, and testing demand when samples arrive. The eventual samples and Bowerman partnership show why maintaining readiness matters, but the delay also supports caution. Make clear which part is your advice and which event in the reading supports it.

grammar.title: Adjectives & Sense Verbs
goals: Put adjectives before nouns to describe them.
Adjectives do not have a plural form and never take “‐s”.
After be verbs and sense verbs (look, taste, feel, smell, sound, seem), use adjectives—not adverbs.
Use sequence words like First, Next, In addition, and Finally to organize ideas; add a comma after most of them at the start of a sentence.
grammar.pacing: 老师根据掌握情况调整语法进度；阅读范围按本课大纲执行。
examples: The shoes look comfortable. → 感官动词后用形容词。
First, describe the problem. → 句首顺序词后加逗号。
The shoe feels soft. / The runner runs quickly. → feels 后用形容词 soft；修饰动作 runs 用副词 quickly。
× Two reds shoes. → ✓ Two red shoes. → 形容词放在名词前，本身不加复数 s。
First, describe the shoe. Next, explain your opinion. Finally, check your sentences. → 顺序词帮助组织表达。

exercises.explanation: sounds 后描述 idea 的性质，使用形容词 interesting。
形容词修饰名词，本身不因名词复数而加 s。
修饰动作 runs 使用方式副词 quickly；look/feel 等感官动词后描述性质则用形容词。

notes.heading: 精读范围 · 按老师大纲
notes.text: Part 1 1965

notes.heading: 课前准备 · 系统学习建议
notes.text: 读完本课指定章节，用自己的话整理主要事件、人物的选择及其原因。补充问题仅用于帮助理解，不代表老师布置的作业。

questions.text: How does Johnson become involved in selling Tigers in 1965, and why does Knight hesitate about employing him full-time?
questions.reference_answer: After trying the shoes and seeing other runners’ interest, Johnson seeks an opportunity to sell them and accepts commission work. His enthusiasm grows toward a full-time commitment, but Knight is worried about debt and negative cash flow. Strong sales interest does not by itself mean the company can safely support another full-time employee.

questions.text: What do Johnson’s frequent, detailed letters reveal about him? How does Knight’s limited response affect their working relationship?
questions.reference_answer: The letters show Johnson’s energy, emotional investment, and desire for connection or guidance. Knight’s sparse replies leave him considerable freedom but can also leave his need for recognition unanswered. Explain both sides with the correspondence rather than assuming that silence means Knight does not value his work.

questions.text: The letters become longer and arrive more often. What effect does describing this growing stream of mail have on the reader?
questions.reference_answer: The increasing length and frequency make Johnson’s commitment vivid and create humor around Knight’s discomfort with constant communication. The repeated mail also exposes a mismatch between an eager employee and a reserved manager. Discuss how the narrative detail creates this effect, not just how many letters arrive.

questions.text: Should Knight give Johnson more guidance, more freedom, or a mixture? Support your recommendation with a problem shown in 1965.
questions.reference_answer: A balanced answer might retain Johnson’s initiative while adding predictable replies and clearer priorities. Greater guidance could reduce uncertainty, while too much control could weaken the energy driving his sales. Any recommendation should address a specific problem in the letters or employment discussion and acknowledge a possible tradeoff.

grammar.title: Personal Pronouns & Possessive Adjectives
goals: Subject pronouns (I, you, he, she, it, we, they) go before verbs as the subject.
Object pronouns (me, you, him, her, it, us, them) go after verbs or prepositions as the object.
Make sure every pronoun clearly refers to a specific person or thing.
Possessive adjectives (my, your, his, her, its, our, their) go before nouns to show ownership.
grammar.pacing: 老师根据掌握情况调整语法进度；阅读范围按本课大纲执行。
examples: He sends a letter to her. → He 是主格，her 是宾格。
Their shoes are in the office. → their 放在名词前表示所属。
She knows him. / He knows her. → 主格做主语，宾格做宾语。
This is my shoe. / These are our shoes. → 物主形容词放在名词前。
× Johnson spoke to Knight. He was worried. → ✓ Johnson spoke to Knight. Johnson was worried. → 两个人都可能是 He 时，用姓名说明指代。

exercises.prompt: Johnson writes to Knight. He sends ___ a letter.
exercises.explanation: sends 的宾语使用宾格 him，指 Knight。
名词 shoes 前使用形容词性物主代词 their。

exercises.prompt: Which sentence clearly says Johnson was worried?
options: Johnson spoke to Knight. He was worried.
Johnson spoke to Knight. Johnson was worried.
Johnson spoke to Knight. His was worried.
exercises.explanation: 重复姓名可消除 He 的指代歧义；His 不能在这里代替主语。

notes.heading: 精读范围 · 按老师大纲
notes.text: Part 1 1966

notes.heading: 课前准备 · 系统学习建议
notes.text: 读完本课指定章节，用自己的话整理主要事件、人物的选择及其原因。补充问题仅用于帮助理解，不代表老师布置的作业。

questions.text: How do Johnson’s expanding sales and retail store change Blue Ribbon’s position as its Onitsuka contract approaches renewal?
questions.reference_answer: Johnson builds customers across a wider territory and creates a retail space where runners gather. These efforts strengthen Blue Ribbon’s claim to be a serious distributor, but distribution rights remain uncertain and another distributor threatens its position. Connect the store and sales work to the contract problem without assuming growth removes that dependence.

questions.text: Why does Johnson make his store a gathering place for runners rather than merely a place to buy shoes? What does this reveal about his priorities?
questions.reference_answer: Comfortable chairs, books, and opportunities to talk make the store a community for runners. This fits Johnson’s deep identification with the sport and his wish to serve people whose interests he shares. The store can build trust and repeat relationships as well as immediate sales; distinguish this interpretation from a guaranteed financial result.

questions.text: What do the chairs and running books in Johnson’s store add to the description? Explain why these details matter.
questions.reference_answer: These objects make the store feel welcoming and personal, giving concrete form to the idea of a runners’ community. Books from Johnson’s own collection show personal commitment. The details help readers see his values through actions and surroundings rather than through a label such as “dedicated.”

questions.text: By the end of 1966, Knight needs someone to build an East Coast operation. Is relying on Johnson a sensible choice? Use a strength and a concern from this chapter.
questions.reference_answer: Johnson’s energy, initiative, customer knowledge, and commitment make him a plausible choice for a difficult new operation. Yet the demand is large, communication is weak, and relocation places a personal burden on him. Weigh evidence available in 1966 rather than using the later outcome to make the decision seem inevitable.

grammar.title: Simple Present Tense
goals: Use the simple present for daily habits, general truths, and step‐by‐step instructions.
Add “‐s” or “‐es” to verbs for he/she/it, and learn the spelling rules.
Review present be verbs: am, is, are.
Write negative sentences: use do not/does not + base verb for action verbs; use am not/is not/are not for be verbs.
Tell “There are” (shows existence) apart from “They are” (refers to things already mentioned).
grammar.pacing: 老师根据掌握情况调整语法进度；阅读范围按本课大纲执行。
examples: She sells shoes every day. → 第三人称单数加 s。
He does not work here. → does not 后接动词原形。
She watches races. / He studies shoes. → watch 加 es；study 变 y 为 i 再加 es。
He is not ready. / He does not work here. → be 的否定直接加 not；实义动词借助 does not。
There are two shoes on the table. They are new. → There are 引出事物；They are 指前面提到的鞋。
He trains every morning. / Water freezes at 0°C. / First, open the box. → 一般现在时可用于习惯、事实或步骤说明。

exercises.explanation: 一般现在时，主语 he，谓语使用 sells。

exercises.prompt: She does not ___ in this office.
exercises.explanation: does not 后使用动词原形 work。
主语 she，study 以辅音字母 + y 结尾，变 y 为 i 再加 es。

exercises.prompt: There are two shoes on the table. ___ are new.
exercises.explanation: 已提到的两只鞋用 They 回指；There are 用来引出事物存在。

notes.heading: 精读范围 · 按老师大纲
notes.text: Part 1 1967

notes.heading: 课前准备 · 系统学习建议
notes.text: 读完本课指定章节，用自己的话整理主要事件、人物的选择及其原因。补充问题仅用于帮助理解，不代表老师布置的作业。

questions.text: What happens when Johnson is asked to move east in 1967? Explain his demands and how Knight handles the disagreement.
questions.reference_answer: Johnson objects to another major demand on his life and seeks greater financial reward and a stronger position in the company. Knight initially delays the difficult conversation, and the disagreement forces negotiation over expectations and compensation. Explain how the eventual arrangement keeps the relationship going without reducing the conflict to simple disloyalty.

questions.text: How does Woodell’s arrival broaden Knight’s understanding of what makes someone valuable to Blue Ribbon?
questions.reference_answer: Woodell brings determination, practical ability, and commitment that Knight comes to rely on. His wheelchair does not define the limit of what he contributes. Use a concrete workplace action or interaction to explain how Knight learns to value his capabilities, rather than making unsupported general claims about disability.

questions.text: How does Knight’s admission that he delayed telling Johnson the whole plan affect the way we judge him as a narrator and manager?
questions.reference_answer: By acknowledging his avoidance, Knight exposes a weakness rather than presenting himself as consistently decisive. This can create a self-critical, sometimes humorous narrative voice and help explain why the conflict becomes harder. The admission may increase trust in his willingness to criticize himself without making his management choice automatically wise.

questions.text: Does dedication give an employee a fair claim to more pay or partnership? Discuss Johnson’s case using his contribution and the company’s limits.
questions.reference_answer: Johnson’s sales work and willingness to relocate support his desire for recognition and better compensation. The young company also faces limited resources and questions about ownership. A strong answer weighs these interests and proposes a fair principle or compromise; either conclusion can be supported by the chapter.

grammar.title: Simple Sentences, Compound Sentences, Articles
goals: A simple sentence has at least one subject–verb pair.
A compound sentence joins two complete sentences with and, but, so, or or; place a comma before the conjunction.
Use commas to separate three or more items in a list, and keep all items in the same grammatical form.
Use “a/an” for singular countable nouns in general meaning; “the” for specific nouns; no article for plural countable and non‐count nouns in general meaning.
Read a Shoe Dog passage, find articles, compound sentences, and lists in the text, then imitate the style in writing.
grammar.pacing: 老师根据掌握情况调整语法进度；阅读范围按本课大纲执行。
examples: The shop is small, but the team is ambitious. → 逗号 + but 连接完整句。
They need a box. The box is empty. → 首次泛指用 a，再次特指用 the。
She designs and tests shoes. → 一个主语带两个动词，仍是简单句。
The shoe is light, so the runner likes it. → 两个完整句用逗号 + so 连接，说明结果。
They sell shoes, socks, and bags. → 列表项目保持名词形式，并用逗号分隔。
A runner needs shoes. The runner checks the fit. Water is essential. → a 泛指单个；the 特指；一般意义的复数或不可数名词常用零冠词。

options: The team works hard, and sales grow.
exercises.explanation: and 两边都是完整句，连接时在 and 前加逗号。
umbrella 是可数单数，以元音音素开头，泛指用 an。

options: She designs shoes, and he tests them.
She designs shoes because he needs them.
exercises.explanation: A 只有一个主语 she 与并列谓语；B 是并列句；C 含 because 从句。

options: They sell shoes, socks, and bags.
They sell shoes, running, and to swim.
They sell shoe, sock, and a bags.
exercises.explanation: 同一列表中的项目保持相同语法形式；这里都用复数名词。

notes.heading: 精读范围 · 按老师大纲
notes.text: Part 1 1968

notes.heading: 课前准备 · 系统学习建议
notes.text: 读完本课指定章节，用自己的话整理主要事件、人物的选择及其原因。补充问题仅用于帮助理解，不代表老师布置的作业。

questions.text: Why does Knight leave Price Waterhouse for teaching in 1968? How does this decision support his work on Blue Ribbon?
questions.reference_answer: Teaching offers a salary with a schedule that leaves more time for Blue Ribbon than the demanding accounting job. The move allows Knight to redirect time toward the venture while still earning income. Explain the balance he is trying to achieve rather than saying he immediately abandons every source of security.

questions.text: What does Knight’s growing relationship with Penny reveal about a side of his life beyond the business?
questions.reference_answer: The courtship and marriage reveal affection, vulnerability, and the possibility of a shared personal life alongside his business focus. Penny is a person with her own responses and choices, not merely a resource for the company. Use an interaction from the chapter to show how the relationship expands our view of Knight.

questions.text: How does placing personal events such as Knight’s wedding alongside business events change the tone of the chapter?
questions.reference_answer: The personal events provide warmth and a different measure of progress from contracts, work hours, and sales. The mixture reminds the reader that the venture develops within a life that includes relationships and family. Explain the effect of one scene rather than just listing business and personal events.

questions.text: Is Knight’s change of job a careful compromise or another step toward an unbalanced life? Support your view with two details from 1968.
questions.reference_answer: The salary and available time support the argument that teaching is a practical compromise. His desire to devote more and more attention to Blue Ribbon supports concern about imbalance. A thoughtful response can recognize both and explain which details carry more weight in its judgment.

grammar.title: Simple Past Tense (Affirmative)
goals: Use the simple past for past events, storytelling, biographies, and lab reports.
Add “‐ed” or “‐d” to regular verbs, and learn the spelling rules (e.g., change y to i before ‐ed).
Memorize common irregular verbs: become–became, go–went, have–had, see–saw.
Past be verbs: was for I/he/she/it; were for you/we/they.
Add a comma after past time words (yesterday, last, ago) at the beginning of a sentence.
grammar.pacing: 老师根据掌握情况调整语法进度；阅读范围按本课大纲执行。
examples: They opened a shop. → 规则动词过去式 opened。
He went to Japan. → go 的过去式是 went。
They tried a new design. / They liked the result. → try 变 y 为 i 加 ed；like 直接加 d。
He became a runner. / He had an idea. / He saw a race. → become、have、see 的过去式分别是 became、had、saw。
I was tired. / They were excited. → I/he/she/it 用 was；you/we/they 用 were。

exercises.explanation: Last year 表示过去，使用 opened。
过去时中主语 we 对应 were。
try 以辅音字母 + y 结尾，过去式变 y 为 i 再加 ed。

notes.heading: 精读范围 · 按老师大纲
notes.text: Part 1 1969

notes.heading: 课前准备 · 系统学习建议
notes.text: 读完本课指定章节，用自己的话整理主要事件、人物的选择及其原因。补充问题仅用于帮助理解，不代表老师布置的作业。

questions.text: How does Blue Ribbon’s growing sales team help the company expand in 1969? What problem remains despite the increase in sales?
questions.reference_answer: Committed representatives, many with running backgrounds, travel to meets and sell on commission. Their efforts expand reach and revenue, but the business still faces pressure from financing, organizational demands, and its dependence on suppliers. Explain a remaining problem actually shown in 1969 rather than importing the later bank crisis.

questions.text: How does the birth of Matthew change the responsibilities Knight must balance?
questions.reference_answer: Knight now has obligations to Penny and a new child as well as employees and the business. His gratitude and concern about the company sit alongside a growing responsibility to his family. A supported answer explains why a business decision can now have consequences beyond Knight personally.

questions.text: The chapter puts moments of gratitude beside difficult messages and business problems. How does this contrast shape the mood?
questions.reference_answer: The movement from family gratitude and rising sales to troubling correspondence or management demands prevents a simple celebration of growth. It shows how quickly reassurance can give way to pressure. Explain the effect through one change of mood in the chapter.

questions.text: What should Knight prioritize as the team grows: more sales, clearer communication, or stronger organization? Use a specific 1969 event to defend your choice.
questions.reference_answer: Any choice can work if it addresses a demonstrated need. Commission sales show the value of reach; employee disagreement shows the cost of unclear expectations; a larger operation requires coordination. Explain how your priority would help and identify a limitation instead of treating it as a solution to every problem.

lessons.title: Simple Past Tense (Negative), Adverbs of Manner & Time Clauses

grammar.title: Simple Past Tense (Negative), Adverbs of Manner & Time Clauses
goals: Negative past: did not + base verb for action verbs; was not/were not for be verbs.
Most adverbs of manner end in “‐ly” and answer “How?”, e.g., quickly, carefully.
Note: well, hard, and fast are adverbs of manner without “‐ly”.
Use before, after, when, and as soon as to introduce time clauses.
A time clause cannot stand alone. Add a comma if it starts the sentence; no comma if it ends the sentence.
grammar.pacing: 老师根据掌握情况调整语法进度；阅读范围按本课大纲执行。
examples: He did not sell the shoes. → did not 后接原形。
After the meeting ended, they worked carefully. → 时间从句在前加逗号；carefully 表示方式。
He was not ready. / They were not late. → be 的过去否定使用 was not / were not。
She works carefully. / He runs fast. / They work hard. / She performs well. → 方式副词回答“怎样”；fast、hard、well 不加 ly。
Before they left, they checked the shoes. / They checked the shoes before they left. → 时间从句在前加逗号，在后通常不加。
× After the meeting ended. → ✓ After the meeting ended, they went home. → 时间从句必须配上主句。

exercises.explanation: did 已表示过去时，后面使用原形 send。

options: When the meeting ended, they left.
exercises.explanation: When 引导的时间从句不能独立成句，需要主句。
fast 和 hard 本身可作方式副词；hardly 意为“几乎不”，不等于努力。

options: Before they left, they checked the shoes.
Before they left they, checked the shoes.
Before, they left they checked the shoes.
exercises.explanation: 完整的时间从句 Before they left 放句首，后接逗号再接主句。

notes.heading: 精读范围 · 按老师大纲
notes.text: Part 1 1970

notes.heading: 课前准备 · 系统学习建议
notes.text: 读完本课指定章节，用自己的话整理主要事件、人物的选择及其原因。补充问题仅用于帮助理解，不代表老师布置的作业。

questions.text: Why does rising demand fail to solve Blue Ribbon’s cash problem in 1970? Explain the financing options Knight explores.
questions.reference_answer: The company must pay for inventory and growth before enough cash returns, so higher demand can increase the money it needs. Knight considers raising equity through a small public offering and explores support from a trading company such as Nissho Iwai. Explain the timing of cash rather than equating sales with cash already available.

questions.text: How does Knight respond to uncertainty about Onitsuka’s intentions? What does his response reveal about dependence on a powerful partner?
questions.reference_answer: He seeks information, tries to secure a renewed relationship, and looks for ways to keep the business financed. News that other American distributors are being considered makes him anxious because Onitsuka can affect Blue Ribbon’s survival. His efforts show both determination and the limits of control in a dependent partnership.

questions.text: How does the chapter’s movement between financing efforts and worries about Onitsuka create suspense?
questions.reference_answer: Each possibility of financial support is set against uncertainty about whether the company will retain the shoes it needs to sell. This pairing makes a solution in one area feel incomplete. Discuss how the alternating pressures make the reader anticipate the next decision, using an example from 1970.

questions.text: Would you recommend accepting outside financial support even if it creates new obligations? Explain using one need and one risk shown in 1970.
questions.reference_answer: Support could fund inventory and allow the company to keep operating, but investors or financing partners also bring expectations and dependence. The weak response to the public offering and the search for trading-company support show that choices are constrained. A strong response names a need, a possible obligation, and the reason for its recommendation.

grammar.title: Simple Future Tense
goals: “be going to” is for plans already made or predictions based on present evidence.
“will” is for spontaneous decisions, predictions, promises, and offers.
Learn negative forms and common contractions for both structures.
Use future time phrases like tomorrow, next, and in + time period; add a comma when they start a sentence.
grammar.pacing: 老师根据掌握情况调整语法进度；阅读范围按本课大纲执行。
examples: We are going to open a shop next month. → 已有计划。
I will help you. → 当下作出的承诺或决定。
Look at those clouds. It is going to rain. → 根据眼前证据预测。
I will not quit. / I won’t quit. → will not 可缩写为 won’t。
She is not going to travel. / She isn’t going to travel. → going to 结构的否定放在 be 后。

exercises.prompt: We have a plan. We ___ open a shop next month.
exercises.explanation: 已经作出的计划适合用 be going to。
will + 原形可表达承诺。

exercises.prompt: Look at those dark clouds. It ___ rain.
exercises.explanation: 根据眼前的云作预测，可用 is going to + 动词原形。

notes.heading: 精读范围 · 按老师大纲
notes.text: Part 1 1971

notes.heading: 课前准备 · 系统学习建议
notes.text: 读完本课指定章节，用自己的话整理主要事件、人物的选择及其原因。补充问题仅用于帮助理解，不代表老师布置的作业。

questions.text: How do the name Nike, the Swoosh, and a new sole design contribute to the company’s next direction in 1971?
questions.reference_answer: Johnson proposes Nike, Carolyn Davidson designs the Swoosh, and Bowerman experiments with a waffle-pattern sole. The developments combine brand identity and product innovation while Knight looks beyond an insecure distributor relationship. Explain each contribution without claiming the name, logo, or manufacturing process is instantly perfect.

questions.text: Why does Knight refuse Kitami’s proposal to acquire a controlling stake in Blue Ribbon? What does this reveal about what he values?
questions.reference_answer: Knight sees the proposal as a threat to control and to the independent company he and his colleagues have built. Refusing it protects autonomy but leaves serious business risk. A supported interpretation can emphasize independence, loyalty, or ambition while recognizing the cost of the decision.

questions.text: Knight is not immediately enthusiastic about the Swoosh. How does including his initial doubt complicate a simple story about a famous brand?
questions.reference_answer: The hesitation shows that a symbol later treated as inevitable began as an uncertain choice. Readers can see the distance between a decision as experienced and its later reputation. Explain that narrative gap without assuming the young Knight already knows the brand’s future.

questions.text: Was rejecting Kitami’s offer worth the risk? Use evidence from 1971 to weigh independence against security.
questions.reference_answer: Acceptance might offer financial or supplier security but would compromise control. Rejection preserves the possibility of an independent identity while making the financing and supply problem more urgent. Either judgment is reasonable if it compares those specific consequences and stays within what is known in 1971.

lessons.title: Future Time Clauses, First Conditional & because Clauses

grammar.title: Future Time Clauses, First Conditional & because Clauses
goals: In future time clauses, use the present tense (not future) in the time clause, and future in the main clause.
First conditional: main clause in future, if‐clause in present simple.
Add a comma after an if‐clause at the start of a sentence.
A because‐clause is dependent and cannot stand alone; add a comma if it starts the sentence.
Do not use “because” and “so” together in the same sentence.
grammar.pacing: 老师根据掌握情况调整语法进度；阅读范围按本课大纲执行。
examples: If sales grow, we will hire another person. → if 从句现在时，主句将来时。
Because the shop is busy, we need help. → because 从句不能独立成句。
When the shoes arrive, we will test them. → 时间从句用 arrive，不用 will arrive。
We will test the shoes if they arrive today. → if 从句在后，通常不在前面加逗号。
Because the shoes are wet, we will wait. / We will wait because the shoes are wet. → because 从句的位置影响逗号。
× Because the shoes are wet, so we will wait. → ✓ Because the shoes are wet, we will wait. → 不同时使用 because 和 so 连接同一因果关系。

exercises.prompt: If sales ___, we will hire help.
exercises.explanation: 第一条件句中 if 从句用一般现在时表达将来条件。

options: Because we need help, so we call her.
Because we need help, we call her.
exercises.explanation: because 与 so 不按这个结构同时使用；because 从句需要主句。

exercises.prompt: When the shoes ___, we will test them.
exercises.explanation: 表达将来的时间从句用一般现在时 arrive。

options: We wait because the shoes are wet.
We wait because so the shoes are wet.
exercises.explanation: because 从句在主句后能构成完整因果句；B 多了 so；C 缺少主句。

notes.heading: 精读范围 · 按老师大纲
notes.text: Part 1 1972

notes.heading: 课前准备 · 系统学习建议
notes.text: 读完本课指定章节，用自己的话整理主要事件、人物的选择及其原因。补充问题仅用于帮助理解，不代表老师布置的作业。

questions.text: What makes the 1972 Chicago trade show a critical test for Nike? Explain both the shoes’ problems and the response from buyers.
questions.reference_answer: The show tests whether buyers will order the new Nike products at a moment when the company needs an independent future. The shoes have visible quality problems, yet buyers place orders, helped by existing relationships and belief in the people selling them. Explain why the orders matter without suggesting that trust permanently solves poor manufacturing.

questions.text: How does Knight try to lead the team after the break with Onitsuka? What emotions or priorities does his speech address?
questions.reference_answer: He reframes the break as a chance to control the company’s future rather than only as a loss. He acknowledges difficulty while emphasizing the team’s knowledge, effort, and ability to survive. The speech seeks to replace fear with shared purpose, though the underlying risks remain real.

questions.text: What changes when Knight describes the break as an Independence Day? Explain the effect of this metaphor.
questions.reference_answer: The metaphor transforms dependence on a supplier into a story of liberation and collective action. It gives the team a more hopeful role in events and connects risk with the possibility of self-direction. A careful answer also notes that the language does not remove legal, financial, or production problems.

questions.text: How far can trust compensate for a flawed product? Use the trade-show response to explain both the value and the limits of personal relationships.
questions.reference_answer: Relationships can persuade buyers to give a new product a chance despite early defects, as the orders show. But runners still need reliable shoes, and continued failures could damage that trust. A strong answer explains why relationships help at the show and why quality still needs to improve.

grammar.title: Adjective Clauses (Subject Type)
goals: Mix simple, compound, and complex sentences to make writing more interesting.
An adjective clause modifies a noun and follows that noun directly.
Use “who” for people; “that” for people or things.
In subject adjective clauses, who/that/which act as the subject of the clause and cannot be omitted.
grammar.pacing: 老师根据掌握情况调整语法进度；阅读范围按本课大纲执行。
examples: The runner who tests the shoes is helpful. → who 是从句主语，不能省略。
The shoe that feels light is popular. → 定语从句紧跟被修饰名词。
The designer who works here is helpful. → who 代替 designer，在从句中作主语。
The shoes that feel light are popular. → that 指代复数 shoes，所以从句动词用 feel。
× The runner tests the shoes is here. → ✓ The runner who tests the shoes is here. → 作主语的关系代词不能省略。

exercises.prompt: The runner ___ tests our shoes is helpful.
exercises.explanation: 先行词 runner 指人，who 在从句中作主语。

exercises.prompt: Can we omit who in “The runner who tests the shoes is here”?
exercises.explanation: who 是 tests 的主语，主语关系代词不能省略。

exercises.prompt: The shoes that ___ light are popular.
exercises.explanation: that 指代复数 shoes，在从句中作主语，因此谓语用 feel。

notes.heading: 精读范围 · 按老师大纲
notes.text: Part 1 1973

notes.heading: 课前准备 · 系统学习建议
notes.text: 读完本课指定章节，用自己的话整理主要事件、人物的选择及其原因。补充问题仅用于帮助理解，不代表老师布置的作业。

questions.text: Why does the dockworkers’ strike create such serious trouble in 1973, and how does the company respond?
questions.reference_answer: Shoes are physically close but inaccessible, interrupting the flow of products and the cash that sales would bring. The team arranges an alternative shipment by air at substantial cost. Explain the link between a supply interruption and the company’s finances rather than treating the strike as an isolated inconvenience.

questions.text: What makes Strasser seem like a useful addition to the legal team? Explain how Knight’s description connects personality with the company’s needs.
questions.reference_answer: The company needs legal skill and someone emotionally committed to defending it. Strasser’s intense response to the dispute and fit with the team suggest both promise and shared purpose. Explain an actual detail about his introduction rather than relying on later accomplishments not yet shown.

questions.text: How does placing rising sales beside a reported net loss challenge the reader’s idea of business success?
questions.reference_answer: The contrast shows that a larger sales figure does not ensure profit or relieve immediate pressure. Costs, financing, and disruptions can grow at the same time. It complicates the optimistic language of expansion and explains why investors focus on the troubling bottom line.

questions.text: If you were an investor listening to Knight in 1973, what would you ask before deciding to support the company? Ground your question in a specific event.
questions.reference_answer: A grounded question might ask how air-freight costs will be controlled, how losses will be reduced, or how cash will be secured during interruptions. Identify the event that creates the concern and explain what information would help a decision. Interest in brand visibility is reasonable, but it should not substitute for addressing the financial problem.

grammar.title: Adjective Clauses (Object Type) & Modal Verbs
goals: In object adjective clauses, who/whom/that act as the object; use “whom” for people in formal writing.
Object relative pronouns can be omitted.
Modal verbs (should, must, might, can) are followed directly by the base verb.
Modals do not take “‐s” and are not followed by “to”.
grammar.pacing: 老师根据掌握情况调整语法进度；阅读范围按本课大纲执行。
examples: The shoes that he designed are light. → that 作宾语，可以省略。
We should test the shoes. → 情态动词后直接接原形。
The runner whom we met is friendly. / The runner we met is friendly. → whom 是 met 的宾语；正式表达可用 whom，也可省略宾语关系代词。
The shoes that he designed are light. / The shoes he designed are light. → 从句已有主语 he，可省略宾语 that。
She can run. / He might join us. → 不同情态动词后都直接接动词原形。
× He must to leave. / × She should checks it. → ✓ He must leave. / ✓ She should check it. → 情态动词后不加 to，动词不加 s。

exercises.explanation: 情态动词 should 后接动词原形，不加 to。

exercises.prompt: Can we omit that in “The shoes that he designed are light”?
exercises.explanation: 从句已有主语 he，that 作 designed 的宾语，可以省略。

exercises.prompt: Which relation word is the object and can be omitted?
options: who in “the runner who tests shoes”
that in “the shoes that he tested”
that in “the shoe that feels light”
exercises.explanation: B 中 he 是主语，that 是 tested 的宾语，能够省略；A、C 中关系代词作主语。
might 是情态动词，后面直接接动词原形 join。

notes.heading: 精读范围 · 按老师大纲
notes.text: Part 1 1974

notes.heading: 课前准备 · 系统学习建议
notes.text: 读完本课指定章节，用自己的话整理主要事件、人物的选择及其原因。补充问题仅用于帮助理解，不代表老师布置的作业。

questions.text: What does the judge decide in the Onitsuka dispute in 1974, and why does that result matter to Blue Ribbon?
questions.reference_answer: The judge focuses on trademark issues and finds Blue Ribbon’s account more convincing, with truthfulness and the evidence important to the reasoning. The result strengthens the company’s position in a costly dispute and helps settle an uncertain part of its future. Explain the limited legal issue rather than claiming the ruling solves every business problem.

questions.text: How does Johnson’s involvement during the trial show a form of loyalty different from ordinary sales work?
questions.reference_answer: He follows the proceedings closely and helps the company through notes, knowledge, and support while remaining attentive to business. These details show commitment beyond a narrow job description. A strong response connects a specific action during the case to what the team needs.

questions.text: The chapter ends with confidence that the team will always have Pre. What does this confident ending make the reader expect at this point?
questions.reference_answer: At the end of this assigned chapter, the assurance offers comfort and a sense of continuity after disappointments elsewhere. It shows how strongly the team depends on Pre as a person and symbol. Discuss the expectation created here without using later events the reader has not yet reached in this lesson.

questions.text: Does winning the trademark dispute mean Knight can afford to relax? Use one benefit of the decision and one remaining challenge from 1974.
questions.reference_answer: The decision reduces a major legal uncertainty and validates the team’s position. Yet financing, manufacturing, expansion, and athlete relationships still require work. A supported answer distinguishes a significant victory from lasting security and cites a challenge actually present in 1974.

grammar.title: Sequence Words & Opinion that‐Clauses
goals: Use First, Next, Then, Last, Finally, In addition to organize paragraphs; follow comma rules at sentence start.
Express opinions with verbs like think, believe, feel, agree, disagree + a that‐clause.
A that‐clause has its own subject and verb; “that” can be left out.
Use “should + base verb” inside the that‐clause to give suggestions.
grammar.pacing: 老师根据掌握情况调整语法进度；阅读范围按本课大纲执行。
examples: First, identify the problem. Next, explain the choice. → 顺序词组织思路。
I think that the team should wait. → think + that 从句表达观点。
I believe that the plan will work. / I believe the plan will work. → that 从句有自己的主语和谓语；that 可省略。
I feel that we should test the shoes. → 在观点从句内用 should + 原形提出建议。
First, check the fit. Then, try walking. In addition, ask a runner. Finally, compare the results. → 顺序词和补充词连接各个步骤。

exercises.prompt: I think that the team should ___.
exercises.explanation: that 从句中 should 后仍需使用动词原形 wait。
First 放在句首后加逗号；主语 we 后用 test。

exercises.prompt: Which sentence still has a complete opinion clause?
options: I believe the plan will work.
I believe that will work the plan.
exercises.explanation: 省略 that 后，从句仍保留主语 the plan 和谓语 will work。

notes.heading: 精读范围 · 按老师大纲
notes.text: Part 1 1975 + Part 2 1975

notes.heading: 课前准备 · 系统学习建议
notes.text: 读完本课指定章节，用自己的话整理主要事件、人物的选择及其原因。补充问题仅用于帮助理解，不代表老师布置的作业。

questions.text: Across both 1975 sections, how does the banking crisis develop, and what role does Nissho play in resolving the immediate threat?
questions.reference_answer: The company’s aggressive cash movements and dependence on financing create a crisis with its bank and the threat of investigation. Nissho examines the situation and backs the business, helping it survive the immediate confrontation. The second section shows that finding a workable banking relationship still matters after the rescue; survival is not a complete solution.

questions.text: Why is Ito’s support important emotionally as well as financially? Explain what it reveals about the relationship between the companies.
questions.reference_answer: His intervention shows that someone with commercial power is willing to understand the operation and defend it rather than judge it solely through the bank’s alarm. That support gives Knight reassurance as well as practical protection. Explain the combination of commercial reasoning and personal commitment without claiming the relationship has no conditions.

questions.text: How does the movement from the banking crisis to Prefontaine’s death change the tone and the meaning of success?
questions.reference_answer: The banking story creates anxiety about business survival and relief at rescue. Prefontaine’s death then introduces grief that financial solutions cannot remove. The abrupt change puts profit and survival in a wider human context and reveals that keeping a company alive is not the only measure of what matters.

questions.text: Why might preserving Pre’s memorial be worth doing when money is still tight? Explain your view using the team’s response in the second 1975 section.
questions.reference_answer: Preserving the memorial recognizes a friend and athlete whose spirit matters to the community and the brand. Knight, Johnson, and Woodell choose to find resources despite financial pressure. A response can support the decision through loyalty and shared values or raise practical concerns, provided it takes the grief and financial limits seriously.

lessons.title: Writing with that‐Clauses & Common Error Correction

grammar.title: Writing with that‐Clauses & Common Error Correction
goals: Write clear opinions using “I think that…” and similar patterns.
Avoid common mistakes: use base verb after should/must; write “In addition” as two words; keep subject and verb in agreement.
Practice rewriting short sentences into complex sentences with that‐clauses.
grammar.pacing: 老师根据掌握情况调整语法进度；阅读范围按本课大纲执行。
examples: I believe that the idea can work. → 用 that 从句表达完整观点。
In addition, she must check the order. → In addition 分开写，must 后用原形。
The shoe is light. This is useful. → I think that the shoe is useful because it is light. → 用观点从句组织完整想法。
× I thinks that he should waits. → ✓ I think that he should wait. → 检查主谓一致和情态动词后的原形。
× Inaddition, she must to check it. → ✓ In addition, she must check it. → In addition 分成两词，must 后不加 to。

options: I think that he should tests it.
I think that he should to test it.
I think that he should test it.
exercises.explanation: should 后直接接动词原形 test。
In addition 是两个词，位于句首时后加逗号。

options: I believes that we must wait.
I believe that we must to wait.
I believe that we must wait.
exercises.explanation: 主语 I 配 believe；must 后直接接 wait，不加 to。

notes.heading: 精读范围 · 按老师大纲
notes.text: Part 2 1976

notes.heading: 课前准备 · 系统学习建议
notes.text: 读完本课指定章节，用自己的话整理主要事件、人物的选择及其原因。补充问题仅用于帮助理解，不代表老师布置的作业。

questions.text: Why does the team debate going public in 1976, and what makes the choice difficult?
questions.reference_answer: An offering could provide money to support growth and ease recurring financing pressure. But it could also reduce control and make the company answerable to outside shareholders. Explain why the most obvious financial solution creates an emotional and organizational problem for this particular team.

questions.text: How does the informal Buttface retreat culture help the team work together? What weakness might it also have?
questions.reference_answer: Frank exchanges, teasing, and the freedom to challenge leaders can encourage trust and quick discussion. The same style can be uncomfortable, exclusionary, or hard to preserve as the company grows. Anchor the analysis in the retreat description rather than assuming every informal workplace has identical results.

questions.text: Knight compares Nike with another son, alongside his two actual sons. What does this comparison reveal about his priorities and guilt?
questions.reference_answer: The comparison gives the company an emotionally demanding place within his family life. It shows that he experiences responsibility to the business intensely while recognizing that his children need attention he does not consistently give. The image makes the cost of commitment personal rather than merely a problem of scheduling.

questions.text: What would responsible growth look like for this team in 1976? Use one financing issue and one human cost from the chapter.
questions.reference_answer: A thoughtful proposal might connect the need for capital with protecting effective decision-making and making time for people. The offering debate supplies the financial tension; family strain or the team’s working culture supplies a human cost. Explain a practical priority and its tradeoff rather than offering a general slogan about balance.

grammar.title: Unit 8 Review 1 (Tenses, Articles, Compound Sentences)
goals: Quickly choose simple present, past, or future by looking at time markers.
Review correct verb forms: base, third‐person ‐s, past, and future.
Review articles a/an (general singular), the (specific), and zero article (general plural/non‐count).
Review compound sentences and comma placement.
grammar.pacing: 老师根据掌握情况调整语法进度；阅读范围按本课大纲执行。
examples: Yesterday, they sold shoes; tomorrow, they will test a new design. → 时间标志帮助选择时态。
They have an idea, and the idea is promising. → an 泛指；the 特指；and 连接完整句。
Every day, she checks orders. Yesterday, she checked an order. Tomorrow, she will check another order. → 先找时间标志，再选择时态。
He sells a shoe. The shoe is light. Shoes need careful testing. → 单数泛指 a；已提到的对象用 the；复数泛指不加冠词。
She has an idea, but she needs more time. → but 连接两个完整句，前面加逗号。
× She check orders yesterday. → ✓ She checked orders yesterday. → 主语与时态都检查，不能只看第三人称 s。

exercises.explanation: Yesterday 指向过去，使用 checked。

options: They need an idea, and the idea must work.
They need a idea and, the idea must work.
They needs an idea, and idea must work.
exercises.explanation: idea 以元音音素开头，使用 an；第二次提及用 the；and 前加逗号。

exercises.prompt: Every day, she ___ orders; yesterday, she ___ one.
exercises.explanation: Every day 提示习惯，用第三人称 checks；yesterday 提示过去，用 checked。

exercises.prompt: They have a shoe. ___ shoe is light.
exercises.explanation: 第二次提到同一只鞋，使用定冠词 The。

notes.heading: 精读范围 · 按老师大纲
notes.text: Part 2 1977

notes.heading: 课前准备 · 系统学习建议
notes.text: 读完本课指定章节，用自己的话整理主要事件、人物的选择及其原因。补充问题仅用于帮助理解，不代表老师布置的作业。

questions.text: What does Frank Rudy propose in 1977, and why does Knight’s response matter to the company’s approach to innovation?
questions.reference_answer: Rudy proposes cushioning shoes with air rather than relying only on existing materials. Knight’s willingness to examine and test an unusual outside idea keeps a possible innovation alive despite initial uncertainty. Explain the movement from an unfamiliar proposal toward consideration; do not treat the later Tailwind outcome as part of this chapter.

questions.text: How does Sonny Vaccaro’s knowledge of basketball offer something different from the team’s running background?
questions.reference_answer: Vaccaro brings connections and understanding of basketball, particularly the route through coaches and college teams. This opens possibilities beyond a company rooted in running. Explain why unfamiliar expertise can matter without assuming the original team lacks useful knowledge of its own sport.

questions.text: How does placing the customs demand beside growing visibility and new products change the story’s sense of progress?
questions.reference_answer: The combination makes success feel vulnerable: attention, ideas, and sales do not protect the company from a large government claim. The contrast widens the source of danger beyond ordinary competition. Explain the relationship between one sign of progress and the financial threat.

questions.text: Which deserves more attention in 1977: developing new products or defending the business against the customs claim? Use evidence to explain a priority and what it leaves at risk.
questions.reference_answer: Product development can support a future competitive advantage, while the customs demand threatens the resources needed to continue at all. A strong answer can prioritize either or propose allocating responsibility, but must explain a concrete risk of neglecting the other. Use the chapter’s events rather than later success as proof.

grammar.title: Unit 8 Review 2 (Complex Sentences & Comprehensive Editing)
goals: Review time clauses, first conditional, and adjective clauses.
Tell subject‐type and object‐type adjective clauses apart.
Comprehensive editing practice: commas, conjunctions, possessive adjectives, subject‐verb agreement, verb forms, and word order.
Rewrite choppy sentences into simple, compound, or complex sentences for better variety.
grammar.pacing: 老师根据掌握情况调整语法进度；阅读范围按本课大纲执行。
examples: When the test ends, we will review the results. → 将来时间从句用现在时。
The shoes we tested are ready. → 宾语关系代词可以省略。
If the design works, we will use it. → 条件从句用现在时，主句表达将来。
The runner who tests the shoes is here. / The shoes that we tested are ready. → who 作主语，不能省略；that 作宾语，可以省略。
The test ended. We checked the results. → After the test ended, we checked the results. → 合并短句，表达时间关系。
× Their team are ready, and it need shoes. → ✓ Their team is ready, and it needs shoes. → 此处 team 作为一个整体，用单数谓语，并检查代词指向。

exercises.prompt: When the test ___, we will review it.
exercises.explanation: 表达将来的时间从句用一般现在时 ends。

options: Their team work hard, and they is ready.
Them team works hard and, they are ready.
Their team works hard, and they are ready.
exercises.explanation: 名词 team 前用 their，单数 team 配 works；they 配 are；连接完整句在 and 前加逗号。

exercises.prompt: Which version correctly combines the events?
options: After the test ended. We checked the results.
After the test ended, we checked the results.
After the test will end, we checked the results.
exercises.explanation: 时间从句与主句合成完整句；这里叙述过去，两个动作都用过去时。

exercises.prompt: Can who be omitted in “The runner who tests the shoes is here”?
options: Yes, because runner is a person.
No, because who is the subject of tests.
Yes, because every relation word can be omitted.
exercises.explanation: 判断是否可省略要看从句成分；who 在此作主语，不能省略。

notes.heading: 精读范围 · 按老师大纲
notes.text: Part 2 1978 + Part 2 1979

notes.heading: 课前准备 · 系统学习建议
notes.text: 读完本课指定章节，用自己的话整理主要事件、人物的选择及其原因。补充问题仅用于帮助理解，不代表老师布置的作业。

questions.text: What happens to the Tailwind project across the 1978–1979 reading? Explain the gap between the launch promises and product performance.
questions.reference_answer: The shoe is promoted as a major innovation with air cushioning and other new features, but production and material problems undermine the launch. The project illustrates how a promising concept can fail in execution when too many elements are not reliably tested together. Connect expectations with actual product difficulties rather than concluding that air cushioning itself is impossible.

questions.text: How do Knight and the team show signs of burnout? Why might success in sales fail to make them feel secure?
questions.reference_answer: The reading shows exhaustion, strained responses, and Knight’s sense of approaching burnout while legal and operational demands continue. Higher sales bring larger responsibilities rather than an automatic end to pressure. Use a concrete reaction or behavior to explain the strain instead of diagnosing a character.

questions.text: Knight wonders whether working harder might cure burnout. How does this thought reveal tension or irony?
questions.reference_answer: The proposed cure resembles the behavior helping create the exhaustion. It exposes how deeply Knight relies on work even when that response may worsen his problem. A response can recognize his determination while explaining why the idea is troubling or ironic in context.

questions.text: What lesson should the team take from Tailwind before its next launch? Recommend one change and support it with a specific failure from this reading.
questions.reference_answer: A reasonable change could be testing materials together, narrowing the number of unproven features, or staging a release before extensive promotion. Explain which observed problem the change addresses and how it could reduce risk. Avoid claiming that testing can remove every uncertainty or that a more cautious launch guarantees success.

grammar.title: Full‐Book Comprehensive Review
goals: Quickly review the three main tenses and their time markers.
Tell negative structures for action verbs and be verbs apart.
Remember the conditional rule: future in the main clause, present in the if/time clause.
Review who and that in adjective clauses.
Review article and zero‐article rules.
Review comma rules for compound and complex sentences.
Summarize the most common writing mistakes and complete a full editing practice set.
grammar.pacing: 老师根据掌握情况调整语法进度；阅读范围按本课大纲执行。
examples: He did not give up, and he will try again. → 过去否定用 did not + 原形；将来用 will + 原形。
If the plan works, the team that built it will celebrate. → if 从句现在时，that 在定语从句中作主语。
He does not give up easily. / He did not give up yesterday. → 现在否定 does not、过去否定 did not 后都接原形。
She is not ready. / She was not ready yesterday. → be 的否定不用 do/does/did。
A runner tries a shoe. The shoe feels light. Runners need comfortable shoes. → 回顾 a/an、the 与零冠词。
× If he will arrive, we will starts. → ✓ If he arrives, we will start. → 修正从句时态、第三人称和 will 后的原形。

options: If it will work, we celebrate.
If it works, we will celebrate.
If it work, we will celebrates.
exercises.explanation: 第一条件句中 if 从句用现在时，主句用 will + 动词原形。

options: He did not gave up, because he believes in a idea.
He did not give up because he believes in an idea.
He does not gave up because believes in an idea.
exercises.explanation: did not 后用 give；because 从句在后无需额外逗号；idea 前泛指用 an。
ready 前需要 be，过去否定直接用 was not。

options: He does not gives up. / He did not gave up.
He does not give up. / He did not give up.
He is not give up. / He was not give up.
exercises.explanation: 实义动词的否定借助 does not 或 did not，后面都用 give 的原形。

notes.heading: 精读范围 · 按老师大纲
notes.text: Part 2 1980

notes.heading: 课前准备 · 系统学习建议
notes.text: 读完本课指定章节，用自己的话整理主要事件、人物的选择及其原因。补充问题仅用于帮助理解，不代表老师布置的作业。

questions.text: What problems does the A/B share structure address as Nike prepares to go public in 1980?
questions.reference_answer: The structure separates the ability to raise money through shares from the distribution of voting control. It gives the team a way to pursue public financing while retaining a stronger voice over the company’s direction. Explain both sides of the problem rather than describing the structure only as a way to make the founders wealthy.

questions.text: What does the visit to China reveal about the team’s ability to operate across cultures? Use one interaction or misunderstanding from 1980.
questions.reference_answer: A supported response should identify an actual encounter on the trip and explain what the team needs to learn or adapt. Connections and opportunities matter, but assumptions formed elsewhere do not automatically transfer. The focus is on interpreting the interaction, not making generalizations about all people in either country.

questions.text: Why end the 1980 chapter with ordinary weather, breakfast, and Knight arriving at work after the IPO? Explain the contrast.
questions.reference_answer: The ordinary routine contrasts with the dramatic change in his paper wealth. It suggests that financial success does not instantly transform his identity, habits, or sense of purpose. The understated ending complicates the idea that an offering is a final, uncomplicated moment of happiness.

questions.text: By the end of 1980, what does success mean for Knight besides money? Defend an interpretation using both a business event and a personal detail from this chapter.
questions.reference_answer: An interpretation might emphasize control, work, responsibility to colleagues, or an unresolved need for purpose. The offering and share structure provide business evidence, while the family scenes or ordinary return to work offer personal evidence. A thoughtful answer recognizes that wealth is significant but does not settle every emotional question.
